To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection device can be designed that is small enough for a person to carry and operate, and that can be used to inject 50 $\mu L$ of fluid at a velocity of 20 m/s.
a jet injection system powered by a permanent-magnet linear motor can achieve a high level of miniaturization by scaling the actuator mass according to the jet velocity and volume.
a portable, needle-free jet injection system can be developed with an injection volume of 50 $\mu {}L$, a mass of 578 g (178 g for the handpiece), and a jet velocity of 100 m/s.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a portable, electronically controlled, needle-free jet injection system.
optimization of portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection systems.
the development of a portable, electronically controlled jet injection system for the delivery of pharmaceuticals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design and optimization of a portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection system is possible and can be done with the use of scaling laws.
the model presented here can be used to optimize the design of any electronically controlled jet injection device, and can be used to design similar injection devices for other applications.
the scaling model and the design of the portable jet injection system are both novel and useful for the development of future portable jet injection systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scaling relationships for the optimal actuator size are valid for a wide range of injection systems, but the optimal motor efficiency and energy density are highly dependent on the application.
the scaling model for jet injector systems powered by permanent magnetic motors is verified and the design of a portable electronically controlled jet injector is demonstrated.
a small and portable needle-free jet injection device can be developed for the injection of a large volume of liquid drug, which can be applied to the treatment of various diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the actuator should be designed to be the lightest possible, with a high energy density, to achieve the best possible system size.
the mass of the actuator can be minimized to a small fraction of the overall mass of the injection system by optimizing the actuator for the specific jet injection application.
, to achieve a compact and portable injection system, it is necessary to maximize both the energy density and efficiency of the motor and power amplifier.
